div.div:
صَفْنٌ [if not a mistake for صُفْنٌ, q. v.,] signifies The [round piece of skin, or leather, in which food is put, and upon which people eat; commonly called] سُفْرَة; as also ↓ صَفْنَةٌ : (K:) the latter is expl. by AA and IAar as a سُفْرَة that is gathered together by a [running] string [near the edge, by means of which it is converted into a bag, agreeably with a modern custom]. (TA.) ―
-b2- And The [bursa faucium, or faucial bag, of the camel; commonly called] شِقْشِقَة; as also ↓ صَفْنَةٌ : (K:) so expl. by AA. (TA.) ―
-b3- See also صَفَنٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
